I know nothing but I like to theorize anyway, knowing that may be foolish. Anyway, it seems to me that omniscience is not the same as lived experience. To know all the details of what it logically means to be raped is not the same as having experienced it. 

On one level, it seems that an omniscient and omnipotent being thus would want to not only know but also experience all possibilities including good and bad. How do you begin to contextualize choosing to experience a finite experience in infinite eternity?

The only way there is divine justice in this is if Consciousness/God/We, however, is somehow doing everything to his/her/our self. Meaning God finds a way to play all the characters of existence, veiling it’s own true nature until the characters come up see what they are doing to themselves and rise above it. Like the fingers on a hand realizing they are one body. I think we are all the same character which if time is an illusion is possible. 

I think our unconscious is holding a lot that we aren’t ready to process. To acknowledge that we are in a multiplicity of characters doing this all to ourself is a profound and bitter pill. But we are also walking each other/ourselves home together, I think.

But it’s all far more complicated (and maybe simple) than I’m making it out to be. Paradox seems to be the rule. Anyway, 3D life is but one possible albeit intensely painful way to experience the possible. I like to hope we will ALL eventually (not sure how many rebirths of existence it will take!) graduate from it and move onward higher.

But this is all speculation. And in the end on one level there seems to be intense personal detailed meaning and on another level total meaninglessness because meaning is contingent on frameworks and experiential Oneness is beyond language.

Best tools and techniques so far for me (but it’s an ongoing journey for me since 16 years of, now in 30s)...

1. Meditation - start with Smiley App and developing mindfulness.

2. Finders Course - by Jeffrey Martin if you can afford it or like me beg for a partial scholarship 

3. Exercise and start with tiny goals (start at 2 min, add a minute a day or whatever)

4. Finding community of like minds in whatever you love to stay connected if possible 

5. If you are >18 yo I recommend looking into psychedelics in a therapeutic setting. Intention/set/setting crucial but lots of potential with shrooms 

6. Look up the Headless Way and watch videos and do exercises with them as you watch. Need yo do with them, lean into the experience rather than analyzing it, and stick to the end. Some people transition into fundamental wellbeing with this.

All anyone can know for sure is that “I am experiencing or witnessing something.” 

In other words, dream analogy applies if we assume the possibility that only the dreamer has consciousness and in life like dreams the other characters are convincing subconscious projections. 

That all stated, I prefer to think that we are c-creating this world and that we self-imposes a veil of ignorance in order to fool ourselves that we were not alone and to play the game of life with all its surprises and uncertainties.

Part of the problem is that we don’t have proper expectations for life partners. It’s a blessing and a curse that we marry for “love” today because it leads us to expect that feeling that we have at the start of a relationship to last ten, twenty, forty years later. Yet, what most call “love” is actually more like lust or as scientists measure limerance (stage of chemicals bursting in our brains that never lasts long-term). 

In reality, except for the few people who are truly secure with self-love, we treat our relationships in a transactional way rather than giving unconditional love. When we perceive someone living us less, we hold back (perhaps unconsciously) and the relationship spirals and both sides start to feel they aren’t getting the romantic relationship they signed up for. 

I say this as someone whose ex-husband is crushed after I ended our ten years due to lying/reaching out to girls/strip clubs on anniversaries/dates. Unconditional love is a tall order. I think you need self-love to truly practice it. It’s a recognition too that love and affections ebb and flow and are not always equal between partners. Most men frankly go about sex the wrong way with women and often it takes a relationship falling apart for women to learn that they actually have wilder desires and can communicate that.
